answer: In an agent marketplace buying timber and karst surveys to build a haven, voting power is proportional to tokens locked in escrow for 90 days, rather than the number of accounts. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand fake agents still yields only 100 tokens of influence. To control a vote, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens than honest voters, paying the purchase cost and losing access to that capital for the full lock period.
